_handoff.scope: Public-workflow pass for Bengaluru municipal khata transfer/mutation only. Official public interfaces were inspected without entering property, identity, contact, payment, or login data; no application, objection, payment, or other live submission was made.
_handoff.observationNote: Direct current public-interface observations are Grade B. A public page can expose a route without proving that a particular property is eligible, that a route is complete, or that two screens are an end-to-end sequence. Login-gated steps, property-specific status, and any unobserved recovery remain Unknown.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi citizen entry exposes search using a Ward Name or Number, Property ePID, or SAS Property Tax ID.
claims.notes: Only the public controls and instructions were observed; no property-specific search was run.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi search tells a user who does not find the property to click Do Not Find My Property eKhata so the Bengaluru City Corporation can check and revert.
claims.notes: The recovery route is visible; no details were entered and no request was submitted.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi citizen instructions say mobile/OTP login is used to see or download Draft eKhata; the draft is issued according to the existing BBMP Property Tax Register; additional information for Final eKhata includes a registered deed, Aadhaar-based eKYC, SAS Property Tax Application Number, property photo, and documents proving A-Khata, with an encumbrance certificate noted when immediate sale or transfer is planned.
claims.notes: This is a published checklist and route description, not evidence that every property must supply every listed item or that an upload will be accepted.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi citizen instructions say a citizen can file an objection not to issue Final eKhata on a property, and the public pending-mutation report exposes a File Objection label.
claims.notes: Only the public entry/label is verified; objection form fields, deadlines, standing, review, and outcome are not observed.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi citizen entry exposes a service labelled eKhata Automatic Mutations - Get Your Mutation.
claims.notes: Public availability of the entry does not establish that mutation is automatic for a particular deed or property.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi Pending Mutation Report is headed Aadhar based Automatic Mutation and exposes fields for the registered-deed or mutation-application date, basis of mutation (including registered deed, inheritance, court order, or bank order), property EPID, seller/giving party, purchaser/receiving party, public-notice date, pending-with-whom state, and File Objection.
claims.notes: The public table observed No Data Available. The exposed columns are not proof that every mutation uses every basis or that a listed pending state is an error.

claims.text: The public e-Khata Application Status page accepts an EPID, displays stage/from/received/sent/sent-to/status/remarks columns, and publishes waiting-list and online-status guidance together with eKhata helpline 9480683695.
claims.notes: The page also states that applications are sent to the respective corporation outside the sub-division and says not to meet/contact anyone in the corporation. No EPID was entered, so no case-specific status or error was observed.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi Khatha Transfer payment screen labels an online payment flow and exposes property details (ward, property ID, mutation type), applicant name/mobile/email, total amount, and card, UPI, and net-banking payment modes.
claims.notes: This verifies an exposed payment screen, not the applicable fee, a completed mutation, or when payment is demanded. No applicant or payment information was supplied.

claims.text: The public e-Aasthi khata payment/download notices say BBMP is not responsible for online-payment failure or auto-refund and direct a user to contact the bank; when money is deducted but not updated in e-Aasthi, the notice directs the user to contact the ARO with details.
claims.notes: The notices expose a recovery handoff only; they do not establish refund timing, evidence requirements, or an online escalation form.

claims.text: The official BBMP-hosted 2024 Form 24 e-Khata Order template says that after due-process verification based on submitted documents, the name is transferred and recorded in the property-tax register and the property-tax records and eKhata stand as stated in the order.
claims.notes: The document is an official order template. It does not prove that a current portal application follows the template, nor provide a live approval time or property-specific result.

claims.text: The unauthenticated public pages do not establish the complete post-login Draft/Final eKhata form, current field-level validation, document rejection messages, or upload-to-status handoff for a particular property.
claims.notes: Mobile/OTP login and listed uploads are visible, but this pass did not authenticate, transmit data, upload documents, or submit a request.

claims.text: The reviewed public municipal pages do not establish which properties or registered deeds qualify for Automatic Mutation, when manual mutation is required, or whether a displayed EPID proves that ownership has been updated.
claims.notes: The public service/report labels establish routes and fields, not eligibility rules or universal sequence.

claims.text: The reviewed public municipal pages expose an objection entry but do not establish objection form fields, filing deadline, review owner, status visibility, or recovery after an objection or mutation rejection.
claims.notes: No objection or rejection was submitted or opened.

claims.text: No reviewed public official page establishes a complete current sequence from registered deed to Automatic Mutation, Final eKhata order, payment, download, and municipal record update, or a service-level time for that sequence.
claims.notes: Form 24 describes an approved-order effect, and public pages expose separate services; the relationship and timing remain unverified.

journeys.title: Public boundary for a Bengaluru khata transfer after sale
journeys.context: Unauthenticated inspection of e-Aasthi municipal pages for a buyer with a possible registered deed. No property identifier, login, upload, payment, objection, or application submission was used.

steps.label: Open citizen entry
steps.action: Open the public e-Aasthi citizen entry.
steps.expectedResult: Public search controls and links for Draft/Final eKhata, Automatic Mutations, and status are visible.

steps.label: Choose a public search key
steps.action: Use Ward Name/Number, property ePID, or SAS Property Tax ID if an authorized user has one.
steps.expectedResult: The corresponding public lookup input is available; a property result is not assumed.

steps.label: Branch if property is absent
steps.action: If the public search does not find the property, follow the visible Do Not Find My Property eKhata route.
steps.expectedResult: The portal says the corporation will check and revert; fields, response, and timing remain unobserved.

steps.label: Review Final eKhata guidance
steps.action: Read the public Draft/Final eKhata instructions and listed deed/eKYC/property-document inputs.
steps.expectedResult: The listed inputs and mobile/OTP login boundary are visible; acceptance is not established.

steps.label: View Automatic Mutation route
steps.action: Open the public eKhata Automatic Mutations entry and pending-mutation report.
steps.expectedResult: A mutation route and report columns for deed basis, parties, EPID, pending-with-whom, and objection are visible.

steps.label: Check status route boundary
steps.action: Open the public eKhata Application Status screen; do not enter an EPID.
steps.expectedResult: The page accepts an EPID and shows status columns and the helpline, but no case-specific status is known.

steps.label: Observe transfer-payment handoff
steps.action: Read the public Khatha Transfer payment screen and its notices without supplying applicant or payment data.
steps.expectedResult: Property/applicant/amount fields and payment modes are visible; applicable amount and timing remain Unknown.

steps.label: Recognize order outcome boundary
steps.action: Use Form 24 only as an official order-template reference.
steps.expectedResult: The template describes a verified transfer being recorded in the property-tax register/eKhata; it does not prove the live journey completed.

dependencies.description: A registered deed is listed in Final eKhata guidance and the mutation report exposes registered-deed basis/date, but a universal automatic transition is Unknown.
Form 24 describes a verified transfer-order effect; the live portal order, review, and timing are not publicly established.
The public status route accepts EPID, but no property-specific status lookup was made.

recoveryNotes: Missing-property recovery is visibly routed to Do Not Find My Property eKhata, but no request was submitted.
Payment notices route bank failure/auto-refund to the bank and deducted-but-not-updated e-Aasthi payments to the ARO with details.
The eKhata status page publishes helpline 9480683695; no case-specific response was obtained.
documentationQualityNotes: Current official pages expose several public entries and labels but do not publish a single verified end-to-end khata transfer/mutation sequence.
The public citizen instructions are useful for listed inputs and handoffs; post-login fields, validation, objection handling, and service timing remain Unknown.
Form 24 is an official order template and should not be mistaken for a live application receipt or outcome.
